sources.title: Nomura’s McElligott says AI is now too big to fail as a $41 billion leveraged ETF bid builds

excerpts.text: The Nomura strategist sees massive mechanical buying behind AI stocks, but warns the flows run on autopilot rather than conviction Nomura’s Charlie McElligott set the market a deadline last Thursday.
McElligott says Jensen Huang’s return has triggered $41 billion in leveraged ETF buying tied to AI stocks.
McElligott’s original setup was a clean experiment.
According to the research findings on McElligott’s view, AI stocks may see leveraged ETF flows reach up to $41 billion in a single session.
McElligott is applying the “too big to fail” framing to AI.
McElligott has been tracking AI positioning since at least that month.
McElligott cautions that much of this demand comes from automated trading rather than fresh investor conviction.
